about: How the speaker's own record shapes an address: the manner of speaking from their traits, the asides they say, how often a name or subject is said, and how far each measure moves in an ordinary year. The order of each kind of speech, its theme and its asks are the outline rows of speech-outlines.json (src/director/speech-outline.ts, owner, Nov 12: 'the problem is the engine'). It holds no sentence: the words are the opening-speech bank's.

mannerTraits.about: The recorded traits that make a President's address plain-spoken or polished: the manner is whichever side the President's traits sum higher on, polished when they tie.

sameRunWords.note: How many words in a row make two sentences of one address say the same thing, so the second is worded again (the words lead's third read, Nov 11: the Vice President praised twice in the same words). Three catches ordinary phrases such as "of the country"; five lets a repeated praise through.

asidesBase.note: How many of the four asides an address of average talk says; real inaugurals run from about 700 words to over 2,000, and a short one leaves out the history and the closing hope before anything else the record supports.

asidesPerTalk.note: How many more asides a President says for each unit of talk (the talk facets' sum, which runs about -2 to 2), rounded to whole parts and kept between none and all four.

namesSaid.note: How many times an address says one of the world's names or subjects (the Vice President, the Speaker, the home state, the year's hardest and best subject) before it turns to the wordings that do without it; a name is said again only where no other wording can say the move. Real addresses name a home state or a running mate once or twice.

subjectsSaid.note: How many times an address names one of the theme's subjects in the same words ("a stronger economy") before it turns to wordings that say it another way; the greeting and the close may name it once more (owner, Nov 12: "good news on a stronger economy ... feeling good about what's coming on a stronger economy ... report on a stronger economy").

redraws.note: How many times a sentence naming the Vice President is drawn again when it would repeat four words of an earlier one (the words lead's third read, Nov 11: the Vice President praised twice in nearly the same words).

asides.about: The parts an address may leave out, and the facets that pull a President to say each: the country's long story, the people met on the way, the call to the people, the closing hope. A talkative President says more of them (talk), a terse one fewer; those said are the ones the President's traits pull hardest, and the part the address leads with is always said.

talk.about: How much a President says beyond what every address says: the sum of their values on the facets that run long, less the facets that keep it short.

changeScale.about: How far each of the country's subjects moved over the year, in its own units, for the address to say it moved a little, steadily or sharply (owner, Nov 11: inserts from the world's records; Oct 27 and Nov 1: no figures, so the movement is said in words). A movement under a third of the scale is said as small, under two thirds as middling, and the rest as large. TUNABLE, checked against the macro engine's year-over-year changes since 2000 (FRED UNRATE, CPIAUCSL, AHETPI, GDPC1, PAYEMS, MORTGAGE30US), where a move of the scale is about the largest of an ordinary year.
